case_number: Criminal Appeal No 1184 of 2022 (Arising out of SLP(Crl) No 1674 of 2022)
summary: Appellant (yoga instructor) alleged sexual harassment by Institute's Vice-Chancellor in March 2019; filed police complaints from October 2019 to February 2020 after inaction; moved JMFC under Section 156(3) CrPC; ICC constituted under POSH Act 2013 found allegations established (with dissent); JMFC treated complaint as private complaint case under Sections 200-202 CrPC instead of directing police investigation; High Court dismissed Section 482 CrPC application upholding JMFC's discretion under 'may' in Section 156(3); Supreme Court emphasized mandatory FIR registration for cognizable offences per Lalita Kumari ruling, noting prima facie sexual harassment allegations required police investigation rather than private complaint procedure.
legal_provisions_cited: Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure 1973
Section 156(3) of Code of Criminal Procedure 1973
Sections 200 and 202 of Code of Criminal Procedure
Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Protection and Redressal) Act 2013
Lalita Kumari v Government of Uttar Pradesh (2014) 2 SCC 1
final_judgment: Leave granted; JMFC directed to ensure FIR registration and proper investigation by police into cognizable offence of sexual harassment as per Lalita Kumari mandate; High Court's dismissal of Section 482 application set aside.
